records.morphology_check: Indicative is agrees with singular fisc in a stated factual content clause; wāt is prior finite indicative.
Sægð is indicative reporting verb; sīe singular present subjunctive is selected for unendorsed reported content, with supplied context preventing a blanket mood rule.
Sægde is prior preterite indicative; wǣre singular preterite subjunctive fits the stated simultaneous past report. This is bounded selection, not an automatic tense-sequence rule.
Hwæt is the embedded object of hæbbe; hæbbe is second singular subjunctive here. Witan+wh is independently evidenced by BT Supplement575.
Saga is the prior singular command of sęcgan; mē dative recipient; hwæðer is invariant whether; plural sīen agrees with męnn; gearwe is prior masculineplural strong.
Hēt command sense: hine accusative actor, ðone fisc separate accusative object of plain infinitive beran.
Gesēo perceives accusative ðone mann as actor of beran; second ðone fisc is its object. The repeated articles are structurally correct.
Geworhte with object ðone mann and masculine accusative singular predicate gōdne matches Cook§173.
Wǣre is a singular preterite subjunctive in a stated present unreal wish; cyning is a predicate nominative. No past-time translation is forced.
Wille+beran is prior same-subject volition, providing a valid comparison with object+infinitive commands.
Prior Unit7 hātan naming takes two accusatives: ðone mann and cyning. This is distinct from the new command sense.
Hēt+accusative ðone mann+plain gān is a command, with no expressed object of gān.

All52 words have productive prior/new form candidates. Hǣtt is prior hātan3sg; birð prior beran3sg. Saga+mē+wh and reported hæbbe have new explicit frames; final hilpst is factual indicative after wāt. Fiscere is new nominal production. Pronoun hē/his continues the fisherman in the report/instruction; the companion is the carrier. This continuity should be explained in prose/key. No citation-only witan infinitive or supplied geong occurs.
